A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReViV study and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–F. Bibliography consolidation changes pagination without removing research content.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments in Section 5, with additional qualitative results and ablations in appendices E–F.

after.justification: v2 retains the original quantitative evaluations in Section 5 and supplementary results and ablations in appendices E–F.

M1.justification: Section 4 and appendices A–D retain the same tokenizers, masked generative transformer, training objective, iterative decoding, and metric alignment procedures.

E1.justification: The pretraining sources in Table 1 and evaluations on ADT, HoloAssist, HOT3D, ARCTIC, and TACO remain unchanged. No task, dataset, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain EgoAllo and UniEgoMotion for body motion, HaMeR and Dyn-HaMR for hands, and the same task-specific participation of EgoM2P, EgoMono4D, and VIPE. Changed citation numbers do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Both versions specify the same two-second clips, resolutions, frame rates, evaluation subsets, alignment procedures, metrics, and training settings. This includes 3,185 ADT body clips and the 3,000-clip HoloAssist comparison subset.

E4.justification: Section 5.6 and appendix F retain the same data, task-specialist, masking, capacity, ViT-branch, and tokenizer ablations. The qualitative case studies in appendix E are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the experimental results. The reporting remains point estimates without added uncertainty analysis.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in main Tables 2–5, supplementary Tables 2–3, and appendix F.3 are unchanged, as are the qualitative results. For example, Table 2 reports ReViV PA-MPJPE 88.6 and FID 0.442 in both versions.

T1.justification: The joint-distribution formulation, token representation, masked objective in Equations 1–3, and alignment assumptions in appendix D remain identical. No mathematical definition, derivation, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same unified monocular egocentric reconstruction contribution and the same accuracy, efficiency, and generalization claims.

C2.justification: Explanations of cross-modal learning, baseline performance differences, metric-scale anchoring, and quantization-related depth limitations are unchanged, including the limitations paragraph in Section 6.

D1.justification: Appendices A–C retain identical hyperparameters, hardware, training times, sampling settings, and implementation details. The code/model availability statement and project URL are also unchanged.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 65 distinct works with unchanged research positioning. v2 merges the seven supplementary references into the main bibliography, eliminating duplicate entries; the apparently added AdamW and improved VQGAN references already appeared in v1's supplement.

P1.justification: v2 consolidates the bibliography and renumbers citations throughout. The main-title footnote changes from 'order interchangeable on CVs' to 'order interchangeable'; the supplementary footnote retains the earlier wording. Scientific prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Bibliography consolidation changes reference layout and removes the separate supplementary reference block. Renumbered citations cause small changes to table and figure-label wrapping, including supplementary Figure 4. All figure panels, plotted content, and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 mainly consolidates existing references and makes a small authorship-footnote edit. The method, experimental evidence, interpretations, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged. These limited editorial adjustments do not establish a meaningful overall quality improvement or decline.
